basis_refs.q: so that, to make a long story short, he feared her, and feared her more dead than living

ledger.summary: Their escort captain is Redhead, who apologises for unknowingly helping Agatha's ruse; Bull jokes that Redhead's wooing of Agatha depends on Ralph's safety. Bull says Ralph has changed his nature and swears on Ursula's hand to visit Upmeads within ten years; the Sage says the oath will bring gain. Bull and Otter ride with them till noon and part. Redhead says Bull boasts of long descent and is perhaps of better kin than any in the east. He defends Agatha as true and valiant: fear, pain and mutual help brought them together. Agatha escaped the worst by spreading a tale that her ghost would curse her killer, which the Lord believed; the Lord's nephew blamed her spells. Redhead secretly drowned the nephew, bound neck and heels with a stone, in a woodland pool called the Ram's Bane two days before the Lord's death. The Lord tortured Agatha but feared to kill her, and later begged her forgiveness.
ledger.geography_notes: The Ram's Bane is a deep woodland pool in a wood a little way from Utterbol.
